chunks: Only those whose scales are heavier in the balance will find happiness.

key_terms.الْمُفْلِحُونَ: The successful ones (those who attain salvation)
key_terms.ثَقُلَتْ: Became heavy (indicating abundance of good deeds)
key_terms.مَوَازِينُ: Scales (of deeds) used in the Hereafter to weigh good and bad actions

ai.seo_question: What determines success in the Hereafter according to the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often linked with its counterpart regarding those whose scales are light, highlighting that true success (al-muflihun) stems from the preponderance of good deeds facilitated by divine grace and righteous conduct. The concept of 'thaqulat' (heaviness) implies not just the quantity but the spiritual weight and sincerity of actions, a theme central to the Shia understanding of divine justice (Adl). This weighing serves as the ultimate metric for individual accountability, distinguishing the truly successful from the losers in the Hereafter.
